summary: Enterprise fintech customer evaluating Dedicated capacity for low-latency chat + reranking. Primary ask: align on p50/p95/p99 measurement definitions across client and server, define streaming vs non-streaming SLOs, and plan reserved GPU footprint for predictable throughput.
notes: 2026-02-18: SLO workshop with AE/SE/Platform eng. Reviewed baseline measurements from pilot (on-hosted) and differences when run in VPC.
Workload: conversational chat + reranking path for transaction scoring; typical request 1-3 turns, avg 220 tokens output, bursty peaks at market open.
Latency targets requested by app team: p50 ~ 60ms, p95 < 250ms, p99 < 600ms for non-streaming completions. Time-to-first-byte (streaming) target: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 180ms.

Measurement alignment discussion: define canonical events - client_request_sent, ingress_received, accepted_time, model_start, first_token_emitted, last_token_emitted, egress_sent, client_response_received. Redwood recommends using server ingress_received + first_token_emitted for server SLI; client to report end-to-end for UX SLO.
Key distinction noted: client-side timing includes TLS handshake, DNS, VPC transit and user device jitter — expect ~30-80ms delta vs server-side depending on region.

Streaming vs non-streaming: streaming SLOs will measure time-to-first-byte and per-chunk latency (95th for chunk gap). Non-streaming SLOs measure end-to-end completion latency and total tokens emitted.

Reserved GPU planning: initial recommended pool = 8x A10-equivalent for baseline 200 RPS at avg 256 tokens (sustained) with 3x burst headroom policy. SE provided perf numbers: 70B quantized p95 ~420ms non-stream; 7B fallback p95 ~220ms non-stream. KV cache warmup cuts p95 by ~30%.

Throughput guarantees: customer wants 99.9% of requests served without autoscale-induced cold starts during business hours. Discussed SLA language for dedicated: min baseline capacity + defined burst buckets.
POC plan: 3-phase - (1) measurement spec + synthetic runner, (2) 72h soak test on dedicated pool with centralized tracing enabled, (3) compare server vs client SLIs and produce final SLO doc.
Security/Compliance: will require VPC peering, KMS for model telemetry, and retention controls. Security team requested SLO measurement spreadsheet detailing what telemetry is exported off-box.
Quote from CTO: "We need guarantees at scale — p99 is the blocker for customer-facing flows, not average latency." — emphasized priority on tail latency.
Observed issues in pilot: occasional ~1.2s spikes correlating with model reloads and cold KV cache; network egress throttling during peak ingest window also surfaced.
Action items: Redwood SE to supply tracer hooks for: ingress_received, accepted_time, model_emit_first, model_emit_last. Customer to instrument client timers and share sample traces (anonymized).
Procurement notes: security questionnaire in progress, finance needs commitment language on reserved GPU count and rollback terms. Expect procurement sign-off timeline 4-6 weeks after SLO alignment.
Meeting artifacts: drive deck + measurement spreadsheet uploaded; Fireflies transcript linked (ff-2026-02-18-9912).
